purpose: WP6 empirical verification of Discord nonce behavior for UNKNOWN_OUTCOME delivery reconciliation, since discord.py==2.7.1 does not expose Discord's enforce_nonce REST field (verified: zero occurrences of "enforce_nonce" in the installed package source).
environment: Real Discord sandbox Guild A, temporary text channel created and deleted by the probe, synthetic message content only, zero secrets/ids/PII recorded.

probe_1_nonce_persistence.description: Does Message.nonce survive a re-fetch (fetch_message / history), as opposed to only the immediate send response?
probe_1_nonce_persistence.conclusion: nonce is NOT returned on fetch_message()/history() -- history-lookup-by-nonce reconciliation does not work against the real API and was not shipped.

probe_2_default_dedup_on_same_nonce_retr.description: Sending identical nonce+content twice in immediate succession -- does Discord's default (non-enforce_nonce) heuristic deduplicate?
probe_2_default_dedup_on_same_nonce_retr.conclusion: Discord's default dedup heuristic held for a near-immediate same-nonce/same-content retry: only one message was created despite two send calls. This is the basis for the RETRY_WITH_SAME_NONCE recovery strategy in did.campaigns.delivery_reconciliation, bounded to a conservative 5-minute window since the heuristic's exact expiry is undocumented and was not pushed further (would require an hours-long live test).

known_gap: enforce_nonce (Discord's strict/guaranteed nonce dedup) is unavailable through discord.py==2.7.1's public API. Closing this gap would require bypassing the library's Messageable.send() convenience wrapper and constructing the raw HTTP request via the internal HTTPClient/Route machinery to inject enforce_nonce into the JSON payload manually -- sketched but not implemented in Stage 09, since building and testing a hand-rolled message-send HTTP path (multipart files, embeds, components) without further live coverage risked introducing a subtly broken send path in the most safety-critical part of the system. Documented as an explicit acceptance gap, not a silently omitted feature.
